findings.title: Stats request that hangs spins forever (no 10 s timeout)
findings.steps: Open /stats, make /api/stats/harvests never respond (browser_route with no fulfil), change the From date, wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: The request times out after 10 s and the page shows an error with a retry option.
findings.actual: After 12 s the page still says 'Loading stats…' and shows no error. useApiFetch/useFetch is called without a timeout.
findings.evidence: After 12 s, main text was '...From To This year Loading stats…'.

findings.title: Stats error state has no retry; recovering needs a date change or a reload
findings.steps: Make /api/stats/harvests return 500, change the From date, then restore the API.
findings.expected: The error alert offers a 'Try again' button that reloads the stats once the server is back.
findings.actual: The page shows only 'Could not load harvest stats.' with no retry control (the only button is 'This year'). The error stays after the server recovers until the user edits a date or reloads.
findings.evidence: Buttons in main: ['This year']. 1.5 s after unrouting, the text was still 'Could not load harvest stats.'

findings.title: Malformed or non-JSON 200 response crashes rendering and leaves the page stuck on old data
findings.steps: Route /api/stats/harvests to return 200 text/html '<html>proxy page</html>' (or JSON whose plants/top_plants are null), then change the From date.
findings.expected: An error message such as 'Could not load harvest stats' with retry.
findings.actual: The template reads stats.plants.length on an undefined value and throws a Vue render error. The page stays frozen on 'Loading stats…' above the previous range's table, so the old data looks like the new result.
findings.evidence: Console: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')' / '[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of render function'. The page kept showing the 1 Jan–31 Dec table under 'Loading stats…'.

findings.title: Clearing a date field silently uses this year's default and can produce a confusing error
findings.steps: On /stats, clear the From field (it shows blank), then set To = 2025-12-31.
findings.expected: A blank field is refused with a visible reason or treated as an open range, and the field matches the range actually used.
findings.actual: With From blank, the page shows '5 harvests from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026' because the server falls back to 1 Jan of the current year. After To is set to 2025-12-31, it shows 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' even though no From date is entered.
findings.evidence: With URL /stats?to=2025-12-31 and From empty, the alert read 'The From date must be on or before the To date.'

findings.title: Months with no harvests are left out of the per-month table
findings.steps: Choose From 2025-01-01, To 2026-12-31 (sample data has harvests in Aug 2025 and Jun–Sep 2026).
findings.expected: One column for each month in the chosen range, with empty months shown as – or 0, so the per-month breakdown is complete and comparable.
findings.actual: Only months that have harvests become columns, so Aug 2025 sits directly next to Jun 2026 and the gap is hidden.

findings.title: Malformed date in the query shows a raw technical message
findings.steps: Call /api/stats/harvests?from=2026-02-30 (or a 5-digit year, which the native date input allows).
findings.expected: A readable message such as 'From is not a valid date'.
findings.actual: A 422 with a pydantic detail, which apiErrorMessage renders as 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range'.
findings.evidence: curl response: {"detail":[{"loc":["query","from"],"msg":"Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range"...}]} 422

findings.title: Long plant names are unreadable at 375 px on the Stats page
findings.steps: Create a plant with a long single-word name (e.g. 70 characters), log a harvest, and open /stats at 375 px.
findings.expected: The name wraps, and the weights stay visible next to it.
findings.actual: In Best plants the name is cut off with an ellipsis and can't be read in full. In the table the row header uses white-space: nowrap, so the name takes the whole visible width and every month and total column is pushed off-screen inside the scroll box. The page itself does not scroll sideways.
findings.evidence: Screenshot scratch/stats375.png: only the PLANT column is visible, and the long name is clipped.
